question: Why does grasping only one relatum fail to yield inferential knowledge?
premises: Inference rests on two related terms
Grasping only one term omits the relation
Without the relation the inference is not grasped
inference: Grasping only one relatum cannot produce inferential knowledge
plain_english: Because inference rests on two things, the grasping of only one of them does not amount to grasping that inference.
